Real possibility ranges over one fixed domain W, the complete set of worlds Reality permits, and that fixed domain yields a single result: modal status is invariant across every point of evaluation, a result the rest of the chapter relies on.

::: {.argument}
**Necessary Possibility** · *The Derivation*

1. *Modal Exhaustiveness.* Every contentful proposition receives one of the two classical verdicts: ◇P or ¬◇P. (§2.1.1)
1. *Global real possibility.* W is the complete domain of worlds Reality permits. ◇P means truth at some member of W; □P means truth at every member. (§1.2.1, §2.1.3)
1. *Fixed-domain invariance.* Every world evaluates real possibility over that same W. A witness world for P therefore remains a witness at every point of evaluation. (§2.1.4)
1. *The Bottleneck.* A world-relative accessibility horizon may vary, but that is local reachability, not the global metaphysical possibility fixed by W. No variation in local reachability changes membership in W. (§2.1.5)
1. *Bilateral Self-Sustenance (L1).* Logical truth supplies a necessary possibility-witness and contradiction a necessary impossibility-witness, so the fixed frame is non-vacuously occupied on both sides. (□∃P: ◇P) ∧ (□∃P: ¬◇P). (§2.1.3)

:::

Together, these results close on a single conclusion:

::: {.theorem}
**Necessary Possibility** · **T1** · *Theorem 1*

Whatever is possible is necessarily possible; whatever is impossible is necessarily impossible. Modal status is invariant because every point of evaluation ranges over the same total domain of real possibilities. ◇P → □◇P, with bilateral companion ¬◇P → □¬◇P.


:::

The theorem is schematic. It does not say that anything in particular is possible; it says that once a proposition has a real modal status, changing the evaluation point does not change the global domain over which that status is evaluated. The Cartesian witness supplies the substantive input in §2.2.

The derivation is also non-circular with the later Necessity of Nature. No step assumes that T, S, or Φ holds in every world. The fixed-domain theorem concerns the quantificational scope of real possibility; §§2.4–2.5 later identify and necessitate the structural content every world in that domain must realize.

The name is conventional. *Necessary Possibility* names the positive S5 form, while the theorem is bilateral: absence of a witness from W is as invariant as presence of one.

*What is established.* Real possibility is global, modal status is rigid across W, and both verdicts are necessarily instantiated. S5 is derived from fixed-domain metaphysical modality rather than from the Triconditions it later helps necessitate.
